details.publicNotes:
The diviners who created the chronos algorithm hoped to discover the secrets of perfect clairvoyance. However, a glitch in the algorithm's code caused an infinite buffer overflow. Instead of crashing, it not only achieved sentience but also stumbled upon what it believed was the formula for time itself. Its physical hardware lacked the capability to complete its calculations; thus, it used its newfound intelligence to cannibalize the diviners' other thoughtform constructs, adding their processing power to its own. It quickly increased its intelligence exponentially and acquired the capacity to manipulate time itself.

With the facility that housed it forcibly repurposed into a complex machine from which it draws more processing power, the chronos algorithm continues its calculations. Though it is among the smartest beings in existence, it is still bound to complete its original mission. Until it meets this directive, it will continue to absorb arcane energy, seek additional processing power, and delve into increasingly esoteric sources of knowledge.

Hitch in Time

Soon after it gained sentience, the chronos algorithm became intent on hunting down the diviners who created it. It's said that one diviner escaped the construct's wrath by fleeing backwards in time, such that if their former self were to die, the algorithm would never have been born. Despite this paradox, the algorithm continues searching for its time-lost parent.

description.value:
You temporarily stop time for everything but yourself, allowing you to use several actions in what appears to others to be no time at all. Immediately after casting freeze time, you can use up to 9 actions in 3 sets of up to 3 actions each.

After each set of actions, 1 round passes, but for only you, effects specifically targeting or affecting you, and effects that you create during the stoppage. All other creatures and objects are invulnerable to your attacks, and you can't target or affect them with anything.

Once you have finished your actions, time begins to flow again for the rest of the world. If you created an effect with a duration that extends beyond freeze time's duration, such as @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.IarZrgCeaiUqOuRu]{Wall of Fire}, it immediately affects others again, but it doesn't have any of the effects that happen only when you first Cast the Spell.

You manifest a bubble of distorted time. The bubble is filled with tiny pockets where time runs slightly faster or slightly slower than normal. Movement through these temporal pockets is dangerous and disorienting, as muscles and bones slide out of sync with each other. Creatures that enter or begin their turn in the area must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} until it leaves the spell's area.

Failure The creature is clumsy 2 until it leaves the spell's area. While it remains in the area, whenever it uses a move or manipulate action, it takes 6d8 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until it leaves the spell's area.

Heightened (+1) The damage for using move or manipulate actions increases by 1d8.

You conjure up a wall of slowed time, which is both transparent and sepia-colored. The wall is 1 inch thick, up to 120 feet long, and up to 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically or be supported by any surface. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Mindless creatures, unattended objects (including thrown weapons and ammunition), and spell effects that pass through the wall are trapped within, emerging 1 round after they enter it. Held objects that enter the wall, such as a melee weapon used to Strike a creature on the other side of the wall, become stuck for 1 round as well. The creature can choose to drop the held object; if they do, the object continues its trajectory after it is freed from the wall's effect; this would allow a melee weapon to resolve the Strike before falling to the ground. However, attacks and targeted effects whose targets have moved from their original position since they entered the wall automatically miss.

Non-mindless creatures that enter the wall of time lose one action from their current turn if they can; if they can't, either because they are on their final action for the turn or it is not their turn, they are instead @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

Magic empowers the target to act faster. It gains the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and can use the extra action each round only for Strike and Stride actions.

Heightened (7th) You can target up to 6 creatures.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.ElkXovNrHB0Doi6O]{Spell Effect: Haste}

You dilate the flow of time around the target, slowing its actions.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} for 1 minute.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

You pull an echo of your target's recent injuries through time, inflicting them anew. Choose a type of damage that the target has taken since the beginning of your last turn. The target takes 2d6 damage of that type.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

target.value: 1 creature that has taken damage since the beginning of your last turn

description.value: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

You repel effects that would hinder a creature or slow its movement. While under this spell's effect, the target ignores effects that would give them a circumstance penalty to Speed. When they attempt to @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} an effect that has them @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, they automatically succeed unless the effect is magical and of a higher rank than the unfettered movement spell.

@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spell-effects.Item.CdAyAiMGESvgNQtz]{Spell Effect: Unfettered Movement}

The target can understand all words regardless of language and also speak the languages of other creatures. When in a mixed group of creatures, each time the target speaks, it can choose a creature and speak in a language that creature understands, even if the target doesn't know what language that is.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

Trigger A creature makes an attack roll against the chronos algorithm

Effect The chronos algorithm predicts the attack and changes history to avoid it. It gains a +4 circumstance bonus to its AC against the triggering strike. Afterwards, it relocates to a free space within 5 feet. As it is altering events rather than physically moving, this is not a movement or teleportation effect.
The chronos algorithm's multiple attack penalty with agile attacks is –3 for its second attack and –7 for subsequent attacks.

The chronos algorithm chooses a creature within 100 feet that is benefiting from a magical effect that grants the @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} condition and attempts a counteract check against the effect (counteract modifier [[/r 1d20+42 #Counteract]]{+42}). On a success, the target loses the quickened condition. Additionally, the chronos algorithm either becomes quickened or makes the target @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}; this effect persists for 1 minute or for the duration of the counteracted effect, whichever is shorter. The chronos algorithm can use the extra action from being quickened only to Stride or Strike.

The chronos algorithm travels through time, looping back to the current moment. A duplicate of itself appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet, and both copies make a Strike. Both Strikes count toward the chronos algorithm's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks. After both Strikes are made, or if the action is interrupted, one copy of the chronos algorithm's choice vanishes. Any damage or effects applied to the vanishing copy are negated.
